defects: Uses [DivisionRing F] instead of [Field F], broadening the class of admissible F beyond what the informal statement ("F a field") specifies — a hypothesis change relative to gold's [Field F].

Formalizes pairwise inequivalence as `v i ≠ v j` (mere function inequality) instead of `¬(v i).IsEquiv (v j)` (topological/order inequivalence). This is a strictly weaker hypothesis: two absolute values can be distinct as functions yet equivalent (e.g. v and v^c for a positive real c ≠ 1), in which case the density conclusion actually fails, so the produced statement is not mathematically equivalent to the gold and may even be false as stated.
Uses [Fintype ι] instead of [Finite ι]; while related, Fintype carries extra data versus the Prop-valued Finite, a spelling divergence from gold.

Conclusion is spelled out as `fun x i => WithAbs.toAbs (v i) x` rather than `algebraMap F (Π i, WithAbs (v i))`; correctness depends on `WithAbs.toAbs` being the exact same map as the algebra map into WithAbs (v i), which is unverified and a nonstandard/possibly nonexistent API name.
